title: Local Winds
source: After the notes' local winds, hot and cold, with standard UPSC facts added

places.name: Chinook
places.significance: Warm, dry wind down the eastern slopes of the Rockies — the 'snow eater', freeing the winter grazing grounds of the USA and Canada
notes: Moist westerlies from the Pacific drop their rain and snow rising over the Rockies, then warm by compression as they descend the far side
Can lift the temperature by 20°C or more in a few hours and melt a foot of snow in a day — hence 'snow eater'
Keeps the prairie pastures open in winter: a relief to the cattle ranches of Alberta and Montana
The North American foehn: the same mechanism as the Alps' wind

places.name: Foehn
places.significance: Warm, dry wind down the northern slopes of the Alps into the valleys of Switzerland, its soothing warmth making them climatic oases
notes: Air drawn over the Alps from the south loses its moisture on the Italian side and warms as it descends to the north
Melts the snow and opens the pastures early, and helps ripen the grapes
Also raises the risk of avalanches and forest fires
Gives its name to every such wind: any warm, dry wind down a mountain's lee slope is a foehn wind

places.name: Zonda
places.significance: Warm, dry wind down the eastern slopes of the Andes in Argentina, through Mendoza and San Juan
notes: A foehn wind of the Andes: Pacific air drops its moisture on the Chilean side, then descends warm and dry
Blows mostly from May to November, often dusty, sometimes for days on end

places.name: Harmattan
places.significance: Dry, dusty north-easterly from the Sahara to the Guinea coast in winter — the 'doctor', relieving the hot, humid equatorial lands
notes: Blows from late November to mid-March, when the ITCZ has moved south
Called the 'doctor' for the relief its dry air brings from the wet, humid conditions around the equatorial region
Its sandstorms uproot trees and its dust haze reduces visibility, carried far out over the Atlantic

places.name: Brickfielder
places.significance: Hot, dry, dusty wind from the deserts of the interior onto the south-east coast of Australia in summer
notes: Named after the brickfields of early Sydney, where it raised clouds of red dust
Blows for a day or two ahead of a cold front; temperatures can pass 40°C
Raises the danger of bushfires

places.name: Shamal
places.significance: Hot, dry north-westerly down the Tigris–Euphrates valley and over the Persian Gulf, raising great dust storms in summer
notes: Strongest in June and July, when it can blow for weeks on end
Its dust storms close airports and shipping in Iraq, Kuwait and the Gulf

places.name: Black Roller
places.significance: Dust storm of the Great Plains of the USA, rolling in as a dark wall of soil lifted from dry, ploughed fields
notes: Hot and dry, it strips the topsoil from drought-struck farmland
The dust storms of the 1930s Dust Bowl were black rollers — 'Black Sunday', 14 April 1935, the worst

places.name: Sirocco
places.significance: Hot, dry, dusty southerly from the Sahara across the Mediterranean to southern Italy, its red sand falling as 'blood rain'
notes: Blows ahead of depressions moving east along the Mediterranean, mostly in spring
Dry and dusty over North Africa; it gathers moisture crossing the sea and arrives humid and oppressive
Its red Saharan dust, brought down in rain on the southern side of the Alps, is the 'blood rain'
Withers crops and hampers the growth of citrus fruit

places.name: Khamsin
places.significance: Hot, dry, sand-laden southerly over Egypt in spring, blowing for days at a time
notes: Its name is Arabic for 'fifty': it blows on and off over some fifty days, from March to May
Comes ahead of depressions moving east across North Africa — a cousin of the wind that carries Saharan dust to Italy

places.name: Santa Ana
places.significance: Hot, dry north-easterly from the Mojave Desert down through the passes to the coast of southern California, fanning forest fires in the valleys
notes: Blows out of high pressure over the Great Basin, warming further as it descends to the coast
Commonest from October to March; brings Los Angeles its hottest, driest days
Drives wildfires through the canyons and valleys

places.name: Mistral
places.significance: Cold, dry northerly funnelled down the Rhône valley of France to the Gulf of Lion
notes: Cold air from the Massif Central and the Alps drains towards low pressure over the Mediterranean
Can blow at over 90 km/h for days, chiefly in winter and spring
Farmers in the Rhône valley plant rows of cypress as windbreaks against it

places.name: Bora
places.significance: Cold, gusty north-easterly falling from the mountains onto the Adriatic coast, fiercest at Trieste in Italy
notes: Cold air pours down from the plateau behind the Dinaric Alps, gusting at over 150 km/h
Picks up moisture over the Adriatic Sea, so it arrives cold and wet, bringing rainfall

places.name: Blizzard
places.significance: Very cold, very dry, snow-laden gale sweeping south across the plains of Canada and the USA
notes: Polar air pours south over the open plains, with no east–west mountains to stop it
Driven snow cuts visibility to almost nothing, at temperatures far below freezing
The same wind in Siberia is called the Purga

places.name: Levanter
places.significance: Easterly squeezed through the Strait of Gibraltar along the coast of Spain, bringing fog and rain
notes: Warm in summer, cold in winter
Moist Mediterranean air funnelled through the strait often caps the Rock of Gibraltar with a banner of cloud

places.name: Pampero
places.significance: Cold, violent south-westerly bursting across the grasslands of Argentina and Uruguay
notes: Named after the Pampas it sweeps
A cold front: polar air from Patagonia replaces the warm, humid air of the plains, with squalls and a sharp fall in temperature

places.name: Buran
places.significance: Cold north-easterly sweeping the steppes of Russia and Central Asia, often with a blizzard in winter
notes: In winter it carries driven snow at temperatures far below freezing
In summer the same wind is hot and dusty on the steppe

places.name: Norte
places.significance: Cold, strong northerly bursting south over the Gulf of Mexico into Mexico and Central America in winter
notes: Polar outbreaks from North America sweep south behind a cold front, from October to April
Brings gales to Veracruz and rain to the Caribbean side of Central America
